t.2.36.1: As that tiger among men was going out with hands joined in reverence, a great cry of distress arose from the women in the inner apartments.
t.2.36.2: He who was the refuge and shelter of these helpless, weak and wretched people, where, pray, is that protector going?
t.2.36.3: He who never grows angry even when reviled, who shuns whatever might provoke anger, who soothes all who are angry, and who shares in the sorrows of others as his own: where is he going?
t.2.36.4: That greatly radiant one, who behaves toward us just as he behaves toward his mother Kausalyā, that great-souled one, where is he going?
t.2.36.5: Driven to the forest by the king, who is being tormented by Kaikeyī, where, alas, does he go, the protector of these people and of the world?
t.2.36.6: Alas, the king has lost his senses, for he will send Rāma, so dear to the world of living beings, righteous and true to his vows, to dwell in exile in the forest!
t.2.36.7: Thus all those queens, like cows bereft of their calves, wept, stricken with grief, and cried out loudly.
t.2.36.8: That lord of the earth, already scorched by grief for his son, heard that dreadful cry of distress in the inner palace and became deeply afflicted.
t.2.36.10: Triśaṅku and Lohitāṅga, and Bṛhaspati and Budha too, all the planets, grown fierce, approached the moon and took their stations there.
t.2.36.9: The agnihotra offerings were not performed, and the sun vanished from sight; the elephants let fall their mouthfuls of fodder, and the cows would not let the calf drink.
t.2.36.12: Suddenly all the people of the city fell into dejection; no one set his mind on food or on pleasure.
t.2.36.11: The stars had lost their radiance and the planets their brilliance, and the Viśākhās appeared in the sky wreathed in smoke.
t.2.36.13: The people who had gone out onto the royal highway had faces overcome with tears; not a single one could be seen rejoicing, for all were wholly given over to grief.
t.2.36.14: The cool wind does not blow, nor does the moon appear gentle to behold; the sun does not warm the world, and the whole universe is thrown into turmoil.
t.2.36.15: The sons, husbands and brothers of the women, caring for nothing else, all abandoned everything and thought only of Rāma.
t.2.36.16: But all those who were friends of Rāma, their minds bewildered and overwhelmed by the weight of grief, did not leave their beds then.
t.2.36.17: Then Ayodhyā, bereft of that great-souled one, like the mountain-bearing earth bereft of Puraṃdara, shook terribly, oppressed by the burden of fear, and with its hosts of elephants, warriors and horses it cried aloud.
